properties.name: The v0.95.0 release cut
properties.rationale: The owner said "Merge 816, then prepare the release" on 2026-10-30; the tag push stays his. Minor by CHANGELOG's Versioning table: since v0.94.0 main holds only #816, which adds two inputs to the request contract (_meta["reflow2/design_owners"] and _meta["reflow2/seat"], honoured only under --http-trusted-gateway) and a capability (cue counts per caller behind a gateway); a new input a caller may send is a change to what the surface accepts, not a bug fix that makes a silent failure loud, so it is not a patch. Measured against the published 0.94.0 binary (linux-x86_64 archive sha256 58a68c57..., checked against checksums.txt): 199 tools, none changed; 35 skills, none changed; get_instructions, describe_schema and the connect-time instructions byte-equal; the schema stamp equal but for its version (28 node, 69 edge types), so no upgrade doc is owed. Nothing is deprecated or removed, so no notice to the MCP users is owed. The In-your-setup lines were checked on the 0.95.0 build beside 0.94.0: locally nothing changes (the --call door cannot send _meta; a stdio session ignores both keys), behind --http-trusted-gateway the owner key moves the settle hint and the seat key lands on the ledger line. flo2.io gets it only after flo2 #205 is re-pinned and deployed. The binary this box serves is rebuilt after the tag (step 9), not in this PR. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018ibUbMKCS1yK5W17cncp9P
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: reflow2 0.95.0 is cut in PR release/v0.95.0: every version claim moves 0.94.0 -> 0.95.0 (Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, reflow2.toml, AGENTS.md's two lines, the five site pages), the one changelog.d fragment (#816) is assembled under [0.95.0] with the opening, surface, stamp and "In your setup" paragraphs, and the schema snapshot's version line moves. rel:v0950 is recorded, pinned to epoch:v0950-cut with the increment's 1 ChangeEvent and the cut's 8 acceptances, deployed to env:ci, env:container and env:dev as rel:v0940 was, and its manifest derived.
